title.title: Absent from the Body
title.subtitle: Bible Readings — Chapter 112 — Understanding Paul's Hope

s01-2-corinthians-5-1.text: For we know that if our earthly house of this tabernacle were dissolved, we have a building of God, an house not made with hands, eternal in the heavens.
s01-2-corinthians-5-1.note: First state: clothed with the earthly house. "Tabernacle" (skenos): a tent, a temporary dwelling, set against the permanent building of God.

s02-2-corinthians-5-3.text: If so be that being clothed we shall not be found naked.
s02-2-corinthians-5-3.note: Second state: unclothed, naked. Death: the body in the grave, the person without conscious existence.

s03-2-corinthians-5-4.text: For we that are in this tabernacle do groan, being burdened: not for that we would be unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life.
s03-2-corinthians-5-4.note: Third state: clothed upon. Not unclothed, but clothed upon, that mortality might be swallowed up of life: the resurrection body.

s04-2-corinthians-5-2.text: For in this we groan, earnestly desiring to be clothed upon with our house which is from heaven:
s04-2-corinthians-5-2.note: His earnest desire was to be clothed upon: not a naked, disembodied spirit, but the glorified resurrection body.

s05-2-corinthians-5-6.text: Therefore we are always confident, knowing that, whilst we are at home in the body, we are absent from the Lord:
s05-2-corinthians-5-6.note: At home in the body, absent from the Lord: a pilgrim on the way, not yet at the destination.

s06-2-corinthians-5-8.text: We are confident, I say, and willing rather to be absent from the body, and to be present with the Lord.
s06-2-corinthians-5-8.note: Two states set side by side: this groaning mortal life and the glorified life with the Lord. The unclothed state between them Paul expressly does not desire; his hope leaps over death to the resurrection morning.

s07-romans-8-23.text: And not only they, but ourselves also, which have the firstfruits of the Spirit, even we ourselves groan within ourselves, waiting for the adoption, to wit, the redemption of our body.
s07-romans-8-23.note: Same longing, same event: we groan (2 Cor 5) / we groan within ourselves; clothed upon / the redemption of our body; mortality swallowed up of life / the adoption.

s08-1-thessalonians-4-16.text: For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:
s08-1-thessalonians-4-16.note: Scripture is explicit about when: the Lord descends, and the dead in Christ rise.

s09-1-corinthians-15-51-52.text: Behold, I shew you a mystery; We shall not all sleep, but we shall all be changed, In a moment, in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trump: for the trumpet shall sound, and the dead shall be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.
s09-1-corinthians-15-51-52.note: The house from heaven, the immortal body, is received at the last trump, not at death. A traveller in a worn tent longs not to be homeless, but to reach his father's house.

s10-1-john-5-11.text: And this is the record, that God hath given to us eternal life, and this life is in his Son.
s10-1-john-5-11.note: Why call death naked, disclaim it, and groan for the body if the soul is already in glory? We "have" a building of God as we "have" eternal life: by faith now, in His Son, its fulness at the resurrection.

s11-job-18-14.text: His confidence shall be rooted out of his tabernacle, and it shall bring him to the king of terrors.
s11-job-18-14.note: Death, the king of terrors: the enemy's final weapon in the great controversy.

s12-1-corinthians-15-26.text: The last enemy that shall be destroyed is death.
s12-1-corinthians-15-26.note: God's answer is the resurrection. The grave is neither the end nor the entrance to glory, but a sleep from which Christ alone awakens.

s13-genesis-3-4.text: And the serpent said unto the woman, Ye shall not surely die:
s13-genesis-3-4.note: The resurrection morning defeats Satan's lie: ye shall not surely die.

s14-exodus-28-29.text: And Aaron shall bear the names of the children of Israel in the breastplate of judgment upon his heart, when he goeth in unto the holy place, for a memorial before the LORD continually.
s14-exodus-28-29.note: On the Day of Atonement the high priest bore Israel's names on his heart into the Most Holy Place; the people waited outside, their fate bound up with his ministry.

s15-hebrews-9-28.text: So Christ was once offered to bear the sins of many; and unto them that look for him shall he appear the second time without sin unto salvation.
s15-hebrews-9-28.note: When Christ comes out from the Most Holy Place He appears the second time, and then His waiting people are clothed upon with immortality.

s16-1-john-5-12.text: He that hath the Son hath life; and he that hath not the Son of God hath not life.
s16-1-john-5-12.note: Paul's confidence rested not on inherent immortality, but on union with Christ. This life is in Him, received by faith.

s17-ephesians-1-6.text: To the praise of the glory of his grace, wherein he hath made us accepted in the beloved.
s17-ephesians-1-6.note: Accepted in the beloved: our destiny secured by His merits, not our own. The resurrection body is the final gift of grace.

s18-1-thessalonians-4-13.text: But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep, that ye sorrow not, even as others which have no hope.
s18-1-thessalonians-4-13.note: Our loved ones who sleep in Jesus are not suffering, not in purgatory, not hovering as spirits. We shall see them again.

s19-titus-2-13.text: Looking for that blessed hope, and the glorious appearing of the great God and our Saviour Jesus Christ;
s19-titus-2-13.note: We need not fear death, we must not be deceived by spiritualism, we live by faith, and we long for His return.

s20-1-thessalonians-4-17-18.text: Then we which are alive and remain shall be caught up together with them in the clouds, to meet the Lord in the air: and so shall we ever be with the Lord. Wherefore comfort one another with these words.
s20-1-thessalonians-4-17-18.note: Is your hope anchored in Christ and His resurrection? Not a ghostly existence, but this mortal putting on immortality.
